excerpt: CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, your own Python script: any Docker image that speaks a three-endpoint contract gets the whole platform.
Tag each agent with your own id via `externalId`. `provision` is **idempotent** on it: it returns the existing agent if there is one, else creates a new one.
Get notified when a customer's agent changes state, instead of polling. Subscribe a URL, and Maritime POSTs a signed JSON body on every lifecycle event.
Hand a subsystem the narrowest key it needs. A leaked key can then only do what its scope allows.
A persistent Linux desktop (XFCE, Chromium, LibreOffice) for each of _your_ end users, driven by _your_ model.
The agent page streams the build log live under **Overview → Builds**.
Templates are cloneable agent packages; publishers can share them via link or the public library.
Mint a personal API key with `maritime keys create` and send it as a Bearer token, the same token the CLI itself uses.
Pass --json on EVERY command. Success: one JSON value on stdout, stderr empty.
A cron trigger takes a standard five-field expression, wakes the agent on schedule, and delivers its `prompt` as a chat message on every fire.
Bulk import from a .env file (or stdin), then hot-reload
Always-on is a flat add-on for the rare agent that must react in milliseconds around the clock.
Every ready-made template is a real agent framework, pre-configured and one image pull from live. Pick one, name it, deploy.
Deploy your first agent and talk to it, in under 5 minutes.
Migrate from AWS, Heroku, or a VPS
point Claude Code or your Maritime agent at a provider's runbook page and it can inventory the old provider with read-only credentials, recreate each workload as a Maritime agent
